correctness.rationale: The endpoint coefficient is exactly a Dirichlet convolution of \(a_\ell(d)=\chi_D(d)d^{\ell-1}\) with \(n^{2e}\); because \(a_\ell\) is completely multiplicative, its Dirichlet inverse is \(\mu(d)\chi_D(d)d^{\ell-1}\). The resulting unitriangular column transform sends the endpoint matrix exactly to \(W_r=(n^{2e})\). The package's exact-integer replay independently verifies this transform and its Vandermonde determinant. After transformation, the quoted explicit Fourier-coefficient remainder gains the divisor factor \(d^{-k_e-2}\); the Lagrange bound on \(W_r^{-1}\) is subexponential on the \(r=c\sqrt\ell\) scale, while Stirling gives exponential rate \(\log(2\pi e|D|c^2)<0\). Thus the perturbation norm tends to zero, proving eventual invertibility. The Petersson spanning formula then gives the nonvanishing-dimension bound.
